title: reMaestro publisher verification
description: One of these lives at verification/<publisher-id>.json and records that somebody here checked control of the name a publisher id claims, and what they checked. It is written by a maintainer and never by the publisher it is about — which is the whole reason it is a separate file rather than a field in publishers/<id>.json, a document its own subject submits. It says who a publisher is. It says nothing whatsoever about whether their plugins are safe; see README.md.

publisher.description: The id of a record in publishers/. Must equal this file's name without .json.

tier.description: Only 'verified' is spellable here, and the omissions are deliberate. 'official' means published by us and comes from the allowlist in tools/registry/policy.py — a diff in our own repository rather than something a domain can buy. 'unverified' is the absence of a record, so writing one to say nothing was checked would be a file whose meaning is that it should not exist. An enum of one, for the same reason 'kind' is: a second tier can be added without invalidating a record already written.

method.description: How control of the name was shown. One method today: 'well-known' — reverse the publisher id's labels into a hostname and fetch https://<host>/.well-known/remaestro-publisher.txt, which must carry the line 'remaestro-publisher=<id>'.

evidence.description: The document that was read. It is checked against the URL the publisher id implies and refused if it is anything else: an evidence URL a submitter could choose is a check of whatever they chose to serve.

checkedAt.description: The date a person did this. Evidence is re-fetched by the weekly audit, so this is when somebody judged it rather than when it last resolved.

checkedBy.description: The maintainer who checked, as a public URL. A name a reader can go and ask.

status.description: 'active' or 'withdrawn'. A verification is withdrawn, never deleted — the same rule as a revoked key and a withdrawn version, and for the same reason: 'we checked this and then stopped believing it' is a fact worth being able to read afterwards.

withdrawn.description: Required once status is 'withdrawn'. Why it stopped being true — a domain that lapsed, a transfer, a name that turned out to be somebody else's.

note.description: What a person actually did, for whoever reads this in two years. Not shown anywhere.
